article_title: Mantis Robotics Debuts the MR-X, a Fenceless Dual-Arm Robot Built to Run at Full Industrial Speed Next to People

content_preview.title: Mantis Robotics Debuts the MR-X, a Fenceless Dual-Arm Robot Built to Run at Full Industrial Speed Next to People
content_preview.summary: Mantis Robotics unveiled the MR-X, a biomimetic dual-arm robot that lifts 70 lbs and moves at 10.6 m/s without safety cages, relying on its SafetyCore reflex system to work near people.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Mantis Robotics has introduced the MR-X, a biomimetic dual-arm robot designed to operate without the safety fences or cages that surround most industrial machines. According to [The Robot Report](https://www.therobotreport.com/mantis-robotics-launches-dual-arm-fenceless-robot/), the MR-X can lift up to 70 lb. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using the house Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Clear, appropriately scoped, 527 words (within the News 400-1200 range). Technical specifics are precise and consistently attributed inline to their source.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots from disk (no re-fetch). source-0.html.gz (The Robot Report, 'Mantis Robotics launches dual-arm, fenceless robot,' June 24 2026, status 200): CONFIRMED the headline, summary and Overview lead specifics -- biomimetic dual-arm fenceless MR-X, lift up to 70 lb (31.7 kg), speeds up to 10.6 m/s, compact footprint, Pleasanton, Calif., shown at Automate (Booth 1261, South Hall); the SafetyCore 'reflex system' / 'full, continuous awareness of its surroundings' / 'processes the environment in real time and reacts autonomously when a person enters the robot's path, without interrupting operations' quotes verbatim; the MR-1 ISO 10218 / ISO 13849 certification and Amazon backing; the Vannuffelen 'Don't mistake this for another humanoid robot...' and 'MR-X takes that further...' quotes verbatim; assembly/material transfer/package sorting tasks. source-1.html.gz (PR Newswire, Mantis Robotics official announcement, dated June 22 2026 'Today, at Automate 2026 in Chicago,' status 200): CONFIRMED the 'MR-1 runs 6x faster than any cobot' claim ('running at up to 10.6 m/s, 6x faster than any cobot'), the Vannuffelen humanoid quote, and the 'We are not just building robots. We are building the technology that unlocks mass deployment in the real world' quote -- all verbatim. Both snapshot files present and readable; both source domains (therobotreport.com, prnewswire.com) are on config/source_allowlist.txt.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific traces to a snapshot: 70 lb (31.7 kg), 10.6 m/s, ISO 10218 / ISO 13849, 6x-faster-than-cobot, Amazon backing, Pleasanton CA, Automate debut. No hallucinated numbers, names or codes. Every direct quote appears verbatim in a cited snapshot. Attribution is correctly split -- the independent The Robot Report carries the headline/summary/lead facts, while the promotional Mantis/PR Newswire release is used only for the company's own quotes and self-characterizations ('6x faster than any cobot', CEO quotes), each labeled as the company's claim.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and non-promotional. Company marketing framing ('outperforms both cobots and humanoids', '6x faster') is quoted and attributed to Mantis rather than asserted in the Herald's voice. The Analysis section frames the safety-at-speed pitch as a bet ('Mantis is betting') rather than a proven result.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. The only adjacent recent article (2026-07/01 Pudu D7) covers a different company and a different (semi-humanoid) robot; no duplication of the Mantis MR-X story.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean APPROVE. All specifics and quotes verify verbatim against both on-allowlist snapshots. The headline, summary and lead rest on the independent The Robot Report, and safety-at-speed claims about operating near people are attributed to Mantis and explicitly hedged in 'What We Don't Know' (no independent third-party safety/performance data, uncertain whether the dual-arm MR-X carries the MR-1's ISO certifications). No corrections required.
